title: Netherlands Tweede Kamer municipal election results 2003–2025
description: Explore eight Dutch national parliamentary elections on their contemporary municipal boundaries. Select an election for local results, winning parties and winning margins. Comparisons from 2017 onward use documented municipality histories.
coverageNote: All participating lists and votes in the cited municipal returns are retained. Each election uses valid candidate votes, excluding blank and invalid ballots. This is a municipal breakdown of Tweede Kamer elections, not municipal council elections. Earlier elections before 2003 are outside this map series.
outsideMapNote: Caribbean public bodies and separately identified postal voting are outside the European Netherlands map. Some archived municipal indexes omit a small portion of national votes; those votes appear as an explicitly labelled national residual. Non-resident votes follow the grouping in the source, which can differ by election.
classificationNote: Our editorial left/right/centre groupings follow a broad international spectrum. D66 and Volt are centre. Separate parties and joint electoral lists remain distinct; a vote-share change does not imply individual voter switching.
turnoutNote: Official local turnout can exceed 100% when voter-pass holders cast their ballot outside their home municipality. These published percentages are preserved.

elections.coverageNote: The 2017 municipal returns total 10,524,838 valid votes, 8,797 above the certified national total of 10,516,041. Official investigations documented aggregation errors, including omitted votes from Boxmeer and Bergeijk. This map retains the published municipal counts; the national election result remains the certified figure. The Hague’s archive return includes non-resident votes and is excluded from municipal shift comparisons.

elections.name: Tweede Kamer
elections.coverageNote: The 2021 municipal archive totals 10,422,851 valid votes, one fewer than the national summary of 10,422,852. Small party-total discrepancies are retained as published, rather than redistributing votes between municipalities. The Hague’s archive return includes non-resident votes and is excluded from municipal shift comparisons.

comparisons.note: Compared on 2021 municipal boundaries. Earlier votes are summed only for complete municipality mergers documented by CBS. Comparisons using 2017 or 2021 also exclude The Hague because the archive groups non-resident votes with that municipality.

notes: Municipal geometry is attributed to © CBS / Kadaster and simplified for display. Historical generalized boundary files may include water areas. The 2006 geometry credit is © 2007 Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / Topografische Dienst Kadaster, Emmen, 2006.

Population circles use the published CBS annual figures where available. Some archived counts are rounded; circle sizing is unavailable where population was not supplied. The 2023 and 2025 views share the 1 January 2025 population reference.
Rotterdam’s 2010 map combines its January boundary with Rozenburg, which joined Rotterdam on 18 March 2010, before the June election. Their January population figures are also combined.

Each municipal party-vote total is reconciled to valid local votes. National reconciliation is checked for every party. The source discrepancies in 2017 and 2021 are documented on those election views; published counts are preserved without redistributing the differences.
Comparison coverage is checked through the official CBS annual transition tables. Before 2017, those crosswalks have not been added: the older maps provide standalone results without inferred shifts.
comparisonNotes: Vote-share changes are percentage-point differences using each election’s positive-vote denominator. Left/right arrows compare the change in left share minus right share; centre and unclassified votes remain in the denominator.
A missing comparison is unavailable, not zero. Unclassified or historically distinct lists are not silently merged into later parties.
